apple-pay-ios-27.title: Apple Pay automation on iOS 27
apple-pay-ios-27.description: Set up a shortcut so every Apple Pay purchase is saved in Qalta as an expense, with the amount and merchant from Wallet. For iOS 27.
apple-pay-ios-27.ogImageAlt: Apple Pay automation on iOS 27, next to the Create Wallet Expense shortcut.
intro: After an Apple Pay payment, Qalta can save the purchase as an expense. Amount and merchant come from the Wallet transaction; you can pick category and account each time, or set them in advance.
You need iOS 27, Qalta and Shortcuts, and cards in Wallet. On iOS 27 the Wallet trigger lives inside a new shortcut — there is no separate Automation tab.

steps.html: Open Shortcuts and tap the + button at the bottom to create a new shortcut.
steps.caption: New shortcut
steps.alt: All Shortcuts with the plus button

steps.html: An empty editor opens. In the action search, tap the Automation chip — or type “Automation”.
steps.caption: Automation chip
steps.alt: Empty shortcut editor with the Automation chip

steps.html: Under Apps, tap Wallet — “When I tap a Wallet Card or Pass” (payment at a terminal).
steps.caption: Wallet trigger
steps.alt: Wallet trigger in the Automation list

steps.html: The first block says When Any Card is tapped. If you only want Qalta to run for some cards, tap the blue Any Card chip.
steps.caption: Any Card
steps.alt: When Any Card is tapped trigger

steps.html: Select the card you pay with (for example Kaspi Gold). Tap the checkmark.
steps.caption: Which card to track
steps.alt: Selecting a payment card

steps.html: You should now see one block: When [your card] is tapped. In the search field at the bottom, type Qalta.
steps.caption: Card trigger is set
steps.alt: Wallet trigger for the selected card

steps.html: Tap Create Wallet Expense (not “Create Transaction”).
steps.caption: Qalta action
steps.alt: Searching for Create Wallet Expense

steps.html: You should see two blocks: the Wallet trigger and the Qalta action. Tap the gray Amount field — a keypad appears. Above it, tap Select Variable.
steps.caption: Tap Amount, then Select Variable
steps.alt: Amount field and Select Variable

steps.html: On the Select Variable screen, tap the blue Transaction chip under the Wallet trigger. That is the Apple Pay payment, not Shortcut Input.
steps.caption: Transaction
steps.alt: Selecting Transaction from the Wallet trigger

steps.html: Tap the blue Transaction chip that now sits inside the Qalta action. In the sheet, do not leave the checkmark on “Transaction” — tap Amount.
steps.caption: Get → Amount
steps.alt: Transaction properties: tap Amount

steps.html: Repeat for the store name. Tap the chevron on the Qalta action to expand the fields. Tap Merchant → Select Variable → Transaction. Tap the chip again and pick Merchant from the list — not “Transaction”.
steps.caption: Get → Merchant
steps.alt: Picking Merchant from the transaction

steps.html:
The remaining fields are optional. Options for Category and Account:

  • Choose — pick a specific category or account from Qalta. If you only have one account, do that: select it once. You do not need Ask Each Time.
  • Ask Each Time — after each payment Qalta will ask where to save the expense. Useful if you have several categories or accounts.
  • You can leave Choose empty — Qalta will use defaults and try to detect the category.

Currency, Note, and Date can stay empty. Turn on Show When Run so a confirmation appears after payment. Tap the back arrow.
steps.caption: Category, account, and confirmation
steps.alt: Category, Account, and Show When Run

steps.html: The shortcut appears under All Shortcuts as Create Wallet Expense. After your next Apple Pay purchase with the selected card, Qalta will offer to save the expense.
steps.caption: All set
steps.alt: Create Wallet Expense in All Shortcuts

push-notification-ios-27.title: Bank notification automation on iOS 27
push-notification-ios-27.description: Set up a shortcut so a payment notification from your bank app is saved in Qalta as an expense, with the amount read from the text. For iOS 27.
push-notification-ios-27.ogImageAlt: Bank notification automation on iOS 27, next to the Log Bank Expense shortcut.
intro: When your bank app sends a payment notification, Qalta can save it as an expense. The amount and merchant are parsed from the notification text.
You need iOS 27, Qalta and Shortcuts, and a bank app that posts lock-screen notifications. This trigger is not available on iOS 26.

steps.html: Open Shortcuts and tap the + button at the bottom to create a new shortcut.
steps.caption: New shortcut
steps.alt: All Shortcuts with the plus button

steps.html: An empty editor opens. In the action search, tap the Automation chip — or type “Automation”.
steps.caption: Automation chip
steps.alt: Empty shortcut editor with the Automation chip

steps.html: Under Apps, tap Notification — “When I receive a notification from …”.
steps.caption: Notification trigger
steps.alt: Notification trigger in the Automation list

steps.html: The first block says When I receive a notification from App. Tap the blue App chip to choose your bank.
steps.caption: Choose the app
steps.alt: When I receive a notification from App

steps.html: Search for your bank and tap the app that sends payment alerts (for example Kaspi.kz, not a related Pay or QR app).
steps.caption: Bank app
steps.alt: App picker searching for the bank

steps.html: You should now see When I receive a notification from [bank]. In the search field at the bottom, type Qalta.
steps.caption: Bank trigger is set
steps.alt: Notification trigger for the selected bank app

steps.html: Tap Log Bank Expense (not “Create Wallet Expense” and not “Create Transaction”).
steps.caption: Qalta action
steps.alt: Searching for Log Bank Expense

steps.html: You should see two blocks: the notification trigger and Log bank expense from Notification body. Tap the gray Notification body field.
steps.caption: Tap Notification body
steps.alt: Log bank expense with Notification body field

steps.html: A keyboard appears. Above it, tap Select Variable, then tap the blue Notification chip under the trigger.
steps.caption: Select Variable → Notification
steps.alt: Select Variable with the Notification chip

steps.html: Tap the blue Notification chip that now sits inside the Qalta action. In the sheet, do not leave the checkmark on “Notification” — tap Body. Qalta reads the amount from the notification text, not from the whole notification object.
steps.caption: Get → Body
steps.alt: Notification properties: tap Body

steps.html: The Qalta action should now say Log bank expense from Body.
steps.caption: Body is mapped
steps.alt: Body mapped into Log bank expense

steps.html:
The remaining fields are optional. Tap the chevron to expand them. Options for Category and Account:

  • Choose — pick a specific category or account from Qalta. If you only have one account, do that: select it once. You do not need Ask Each Time.
  • Ask Each Time — after each notification Qalta will ask where to save the expense. Useful if you have several categories or accounts.
  • You can leave Choose empty — Qalta will use defaults and try to detect the category.

Note and Date can stay empty. Turn on Show When Run so a confirmation appears. Tap the back arrow.
steps.caption: Category, account, and confirmation
steps.alt: Category, Account, and Show When Run

steps.html: The shortcut appears under All Shortcuts as Log Bank Expense. After the next payment notification from that bank app, Qalta will offer to save the expense.
steps.caption: All set
steps.alt: Log Bank Expense in All Shortcuts

apple-pay-ios-26.title: Apple Pay automation on iOS 26
apple-pay-ios-26.description: Set up a Shortcuts automation so every Apple Pay purchase is saved in Qalta as an expense, with the amount and merchant filled in. For iOS 26.
apple-pay-ios-26.ogImageAlt: Apple Pay automation on iOS 26, next to the Create Wallet Expense action in Shortcuts.
intro: After an Apple Pay payment, Qalta can save the purchase as an expense. Amount and merchant come from the transaction; you can pick category and account each time, or set them in advance.
You need iOS 26, Qalta and Shortcuts, and cards in Wallet.

steps.html: Open Settings → Wallet & Apple Pay. Turn on Live Activities and Cellular Data.
steps.caption: Wallet permissions
steps.alt: Wallet and Apple Pay permissions

steps.html: Open Shortcuts, go to the Automation tab, and tap New Automation.
steps.caption: New automation
steps.alt: Shortcuts Automation tab

steps.html: Choose Wallet — “When I tap a Wallet Card or Pass” (payment at a terminal).
steps.caption: Wallet trigger
steps.alt: Wallet trigger in the automation list

steps.html: Select the cards you want Qalta to track. Tap Next.
steps.caption: Which cards to track
steps.alt: Selecting payment cards

steps.html: Keep the Wallet categories you care about (all is fine). Select Run Immediately (not Run After Confirmation). Tap Next.
steps.caption: Categories
steps.alt: Wallet categories

steps.html: On the tile screen, tap the gray Create New Shortcut card at the top left. Do not pick an existing shortcut from the list below.
steps.caption: New shortcut
steps.alt: Create New Shortcut tile

steps.html: An empty editor opens. In the action search at the bottom, type Qalta and tap Create Wallet Expense (not “Create Transaction”).
steps.caption: Qalta action
steps.alt: Searching for Create Wallet Expense

steps.html: You should see two blocks: “Receive transaction as input” and the Qalta action. Tap the gray Amount field in the Qalta action — a keypad appears. Above it, tap Select Variable.
steps.caption: Tap Amount, then Select Variable
steps.alt: Amount field and Select Variable

steps.html: On the Select Variable screen, tap the blue Shortcut Input chip under “Receive transaction as input”.
steps.caption: Shortcut Input
steps.alt: Selecting Shortcut Input as the variable

steps.html: Tap the blue Shortcut Input chip that now sits inside the Qalta action. In the sheet, Type should be Transaction. Do not leave the checkmark on “Transaction” — scroll the list and tap Amount.
steps.caption: Type Transaction → Amount
steps.alt: Transaction properties: tap Amount

steps.html: Repeat for the store name. Tap the chevron on the Qalta action to expand the fields. Tap Merchant → Select Variable → Shortcut Input. Tap the chip again, Type Transaction, then pick Merchant from the list.
steps.caption: Type Transaction → Merchant
steps.alt: Picking Merchant from the transaction

steps.html:
The remaining fields are optional. Options for Category and Account:

  • Choose — pick a specific category or account from Qalta. If you only have one account, do that: select it once. You do not need Ask Each Time.
  • Ask Each Time — after each payment Qalta will ask where to save the expense. Useful if you have several categories or accounts.
  • You can leave Choose empty — Qalta will use defaults and try to detect the category.

Currency, Note, and Date can stay empty. Turn on Show When Run so a confirmation appears after payment. Tap the blue checkmark at the top.
steps.caption: Category, account, and confirmation
steps.alt: Category, Account, and Show When Run

steps.html: The automation appears under Automation. After your next Apple Pay purchase with the selected card, Qalta will offer to save the expense.
steps.caption: All set
steps.alt: Finished automation in the list
